correctness.rationale: For the all-shortest-path geodesic convexity in products of finite complete graphs, geodesic intervals independently change coordinate values, hence every nonempty convex set is exactly a product of coordinate subsets; the concept count is 1+∏_i(2^{n_i}-1). A support S is shattered iff each point has a coordinate value unique within S: this is necessary from the leave-one-out trace and sufficient since coordinate-projection hulls exclude every omitted point. Thus VCdim k when at least two factors are nontrivial and k+1 otherwise, k=∑(n_i−1). Littlestone upper bound k+1 follows from the positive first-query version space having 2^k boxes, while induction on k gives a depth-(k+1) complete mistake tree, exploiting a second nontrivial coordinate after a negative answer. For two factors private-value support graphs are star forests; exact max-support counts mn (m,n>=3), 2^max (one side two), 6 (2x2). Independent direct concept and online-dimension recursion verified (2,2): concepts 10, Ldim3; (2,3):22,Ldim4; (2,2,2):28,Ldim4, agreeing with proof.

evidence: Thiessen–Gärtner give generic learning bounds for convex graph concepts and Jiang–Pelayo–Pritikin product convexity, but not an explicit tight Littlestone dimension for this whole Cartesian-box class. General inequality Ldim<=log2|C| is weaker here and not enough for k+1 lower bound.
